verdict.note: Real-browser session menu: live row shows five icon-led actions; an intercepted offline fixture shows four actions with no attach item or dangling separator. Computed chrome is 11px type, 28px rows, 14px registry icons, with destructive close isolated and right-bottom placement clamped inside the viewport.

Real-browser node menus: an overlay node shows the fixed icon-led commands plus its status-glyph session group and two separators; a plain node shows exactly four fixed commands and one separator. Labels ellipsize cleanly, focus is visible, danger is isolated, and no emoji appear.
5 icon-led rows in 2 groups, separator before the danger group, no emoji, clamped on-screen; menu presses are now pointer-inert (focus stays with the input surface)
4 icon-led rows in 2 groups, separator before danger, no emoji, on-screen; same shared shell, same inert-chrome guard

Chromium: pointer opening leaves focus untouched (inertChromePress path unchanged, menu opens with 1 menu node); keyboard opening puts focus on the first command and ArrowDown moves it to the next; Escape closes and focus returns to the row it borrowed from; 'Open in a new tab' prints the live cap ⌥⏎ read from the registry.

Re-measured after the menu moved onto the raised rung. Surface rgb(55,55,55) = the resolved --raised, standing on a sidebar of rgb(33,33,33), a plane of rgb(38,38,38) and a terminal of rgb(27,27,27) — three distinct grounds under one card, where the same read before the change returned rgb(33,33,33) for all of menu, sidebar and terminal. Chrome unchanged and intact: six rows at 12px/28px, every one an svg registry icon beside its word, no emoji, no clipped label, inside the viewport, one hairline separator isolating the danger-tinted close (rgb(213,118,63)). Hover and focus both resolve --wash-hover with outline:none, i.e. the one inset ring. The offline row drops 'open in terminal…' and still carries exactly one separator — no dangling divider.
